None is present to represent the appellant in L.P.A. No. 551 of 2014 although the name of Mr. Mrinal Kanti Roy is reflecting in the daily cause-list.
2. All the batch of appeals is directed against the common Judgment dated 19.09.2014 passed by the learned Single Judge in W.P.(S) No. 3813 of 2005 with other analogous matters.

3. The fact of the instant appeal is that the appointment has been provided on the basis of an agreement entered in between the raiyat and the BCCL, in which the land was acquired on the basis of the requisition made by the BCCL to the State.

The State has also initiated a proceeding for Land Acquisition by issuing notice under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 which had been culminated in the year 1985-86 by passing awards in favour of the raiyats.
The mining work has been started on the land in question on the basis of the condition inserted in the avenue that one of the members of the raiyats family will be provided with an appointment.

The appointments have been provided in favour of one of the raiyats and they were also started discharging their duties but after a lapse of 21 to 22 years, the aforesaid person who have been appointed, dispensed with the service by the respondent-BCCL.
4. It has been contended that the appointment and the compensation in lieu of utilization of the land and acquisition, respectively, have been put on two different pedestals.

The reason for such submission is that the appointment since has been provided in the year 1981, based upon the agreement then why the compensation has been awarded on conclusion of the Land Acquisition proceeding in the year 1985-86.

5. The grounds have been agitated on behalf of the appellants that once the appointment has been provided in the year 1981 based upon the agreement in favour of one of the signatory to the agreement then even if there was no consent from the other legal heirs after lapse of about 21 to 22 years on that count there was no occasion for the respondent-BCCL to dispense with the services of one or the other raiyats.

sentences.text:
The grievance of the appellants is that after allowing them to put in service for about 22 years,
they have been removed from service.
The petitioners have approached to this Court in the year 2004 by filing writ petitions being W.P.(S) No. 6145 of 2004 and W.P.(S) No. 6483 of 2004.

The learned Single Judge while disposing of the writ petitions had granted liberty to the writ petitioners to satisfy the authority by giving details of their lands against which they/their father got employment in the year 1981.
The details have been furnished giving therein the details.

The authority has passed the order on 20.05.2005 but the said representation by way of furnishing the details has not been found to be satisfactory and as such rejected on the ground that all awardees has not given consent in his favour.
That led the respondent-BCCL to the conclusion that the appointments were erroneously and illegally procured by Sri Gima Mahato, one of the litigants.

The same has again been challenged by filing writ petition being W.P.(S) No. 3813 of 2005 alongwith other writ petitions wherein the learned Single Judge by making reference of the discrepancy in the details furnished and the claim of entitlement has been found to be in contradiction and as such instead of passing a positive direction has come to the conclusion by recording the finding that in such a disputed question of fact, it will not be proper for the Writ Court to adjudicate the issue and,
as such, the petitioners have been relegated to approach the forum as per the provision of I.D. Act,
1947.

7. This Court after going through the finding recorded by the learned Single Judge in the impugned judgment has found the detailed description as has been made in paragraph-18 by way of a tubular chart showing the reference of all the litigants who were petitioners in one or the other writ petitions which is based upon enquiry conducted by the respondent-BCCL.

8. This Court has posed a question to the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BCCL who is being represented by Mr. Anoop Kr. Mehta that what is the basis of taking note of the said enquiry report.
9. It has been submitted that the same must be on the record of the writ petitions.
10. This Court when has enquired from the Court Master then it has been informed that the record pertaining to the Writ Court has not been made available by the Office.
11. This Court in view of the aforesaid hereby direct the Registry to produce the original record of the writ petition on the next date of hearing.
12. In addition thereto, the respondent-BCCL is also being called upon to produce the entire original records including the enquiry report before this Court on or before the next date of hearing.

13. The State is being represented by Mr. Indranil Bhaduri, learned SC-IV who is directed to produce the original record pertaining to the L.A. Cases being L.A. Case No. 30/1985-86 which is the subject matter of acquisition of the land in question on or before the next date of hearing.

14. The question has been raised by the learned Senior Counsel representing the appellants that the mining operation has been carried out and only thereafter the decision has been taken to terminate Smt. Mehta, learned counsel on behalf of respondent by referring to the affidavit filed by District Land Acquisition Officer, Dhanbad wherein the specific statement has been made in paragraph-4 which was supported by the photographs and the map appended as Annexure-6 series to the said affidavit dated 11.12.2013.

The same be clarified by BCCL by filing affidavit.
